text:
Alice Chen: quick notes from today's kv quant experiments on A100 pool — saw memory drop but a weird p99 spike when using INT8 KV + fp8 weights. logs and numbers below, looking for ideas :thinking:

Raj Patel: saw that too. basic numbers: fp16 KV baseline p99=38ms, mem=6.8GB. INT8-KV run p99=61ms, mem=4.9GB. throughput ~same for long batches, but single-request latency regressed.

Marta López: decode quality also shifted — increase in repetition for long contexts (>=2048 tokens). BLEU-ish tests show small but consistent drop. suspect calibration/scaling drift during incremental decode.

Zane Kim: profiling trace attached in thread (summary): kernel switch path doing fallback to generic kernel when seq_len changes mid-request. hot path shows extra memcpy and an extra kernel-launch dependency. that explains added 20-30ms.

Olivia Tran: config used for the runs: `kv_quant_mode=int8_per_tensor`, `kv_pack=True`, `enable_fp8_weights=True`, `batching=dynamic`, `seq_hysteresis=0`. no per-head scales.

Raj Patel: two immediate hypotheses: 1) quantized KV layout isn't aligned for our fused decode kernels so we hit slow path; 2) calibration table unstable -> occasionally expands KV bytes and triggers different kernel choices mid-decode.

Alice Chen: i can repro on a single machine. posted a tiny repro script: ```bash
# repro (local)
EXPORT MODEL=redwood-7b-test
python serve_client.py --seq 4096 --kv-quant int8 --warm 5 --samples 50
```

Marta López: looked at calibration stats — per-tensor min/max distributions show outliers in some layers on longer contexts. We used single-pass calibration from 512-token windows; that's probably not representative.

Zane Kim: also saw kernel selection logic: `choose_kernel(seq_len, batch, kv_layout)` returns different code path when `kv_byte_stride % 128 != 0`. INT8 packing changed stride, so we fell back. adding alignment pad fixed p99 in a quick test.

Raj Patel: interesting. so two separate contributors: packing alignment causing kernel fallback and calibration causing decode iteration differences. either alone could cause the observed regression.

Olivia Tran: memory savings still attractive: ~28% lower KV resident size for int8 vs fp16. that helps multi-tenant density. but need to keep latency and decode quality.

Alice Chen: propose short action plan: 1) enforce 128-byte alignment in KV packer (Zane) 2) rerun calibration with stratified windows: {32,512,2048} tokens and per-head scales (Marta) 3) add hysteresis to kernel selection so it doesn't switch mid-decode (Raj) 4) canary rollout w/ regen-check (Olivia).

Zane Kim: already prototyped alignment pad in packer; microbench: p99 dropped from 61->42ms (still +4ms vs fp16 baseline). patch incoming.

Marta López: per-head calibration increases memory for scale tables slightly but reduces decode drift. ran small eval: repetition score improved, BLEU-ish back to within 0.5% of baseline. will push calibration script to repo.

Raj Patel: hysteresis idea: require kernel switch only at chunk boundary and add threshold delta of 10% before switching. also track `kv_cache_hit_rate` to avoid oscillation under saturation. wrote a draft PR comment.

perf-bot: perf-regression-detect: int8-kv-canary failed p95 SLA in 2/10 runs, p99 exceeded threshold in 6/10 runs. attaching perf diffs.

Olivia Tran: for canary we should gate on regen-rate <= 0.2 and p99 <= baseline + 10ms. if pass, enable int8-kv for reserved capacity only.

Alice Chen: next steps owners: Zane: packer alignment PR; Marta: new calibration sweep and upload results; Raj: hysteresis + kernel selection test harness; Olivia: update rollout policy and canary job. aim for internal canary by EOD tomorrow.

Zane Kim: small gotcha—H100's kernel selection behaves slightly different; align pad helps there too but we need a small opt path for `compute_capability >= 9.0`. i'll add a GPU feature flag.

Marta López: also found one decode drift root cause: scaling table quant values were stored as FP16 in the metadata blob and we were reading them as FP32 in some branches — rounding variance across codepaths. fixed locally.

Raj Patel: test harness additions: synthetic seq jitter generator and a `--force-kernel` flag so we can simulate mid-decode switches. will add nightly job.

Alice Chen: thanks all — this feels actionable. drop logs and short perf summaries in this thread when you have them. if anyone can try a small canary on dedicated dev-rt-4 cluster that would be great. :thumbsup:
